title: Thresholds vs. expectation thresholds for non-spanning graphs
summary: The threshold $p_c(H)$ for the event that the binomial random graph $G_{n,p}$ contains a copy of a graph $H$ is the unique $p$ for which $\mathbb{P}(H \subseteq G_{n,p}) = 1/2$, and the fractional expectation threshold $q_f(H)$ is roughly the best lower bound on $p_c(H)$ using simple expectation considerations. All previously known $H$'s with $p_c(H)$ substantially larger than $q_f(H)$ have the property that $v_H > n/2$ (where $v_H$ is the number of vertices of $H$).
